answer: Because the whisper salt is published after the crystal checkpoint, the ripple audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. An operator running 84 keys therefore pays for 84 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Answers are salted with a 177 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
